Algae growth in a pond is a natural part, and important indicator, of good water quality.  If your pond were producing all this algae you could clean it by dumping it on your lawn in chunks as fertilizer! Here’s how though:

First you’ll need to get most of the algae out by skimming the pond. I suggest doing that at night (as the water gets colder) so you aren't harming any plants that are sensitive to the low temperatures.

If this skimming doesn't get all the algae out you can use a skimmer and pump system to remove as much of the algae from the pond as possible.

If this doesn’t get all the algae out, then it is either dead algae, or very little algae that you would be trying to skim out have been killed by high-intensity sunlight conditions that occur around daybreak and nightfall, and since algae generally thrive in midday temperatures.

If you can use high-intensity light conditions then here’s one method:   Build the poles out far enough and shine lights at them from time to time, usually mid day in the summer and late afternoon in the winter. Since algae are photosynthesizing organisms that will only grow in dark conditions they will die from their own over-exposure.

Here's an example photo:  

![Photo from google](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-fB6X6s1zBwI/tT62Z8LZ9C5/AAAAAAAAAZk/E5GnX1ZwBpE/w450-h267/nature.png?cd=3)  

What I have is algae growing very nicely on my sketched in lake waterscape with me casting the shadow from below![photo by kennyk](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-JtE53DpXxwA/tVtKzIw47Xl/AAAAAAAAA24/aQWf5Y4P4Vk/nature.png?cd=3)[photo by kennyk](https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-GvB5Z5N8D2E/tK2J7U74D8s/AAAAAAAAA2E/xG94x94WpXs/nature.png?cd=3)  

As you can imagine this means algae needs to die quickly before sunlight conditions occur midday. 

For this I have two options I could recommend:

### Option #1
Use a flashlight source of light to run under your skimmer basket of the pond when algae grows and is most actively multiplying.

Alternatively (option #2):

If there was time to run skimmers as part of my daily schedule in summer on days with daylight and when temperatures were above 90 degrees Fahrenheit at mid-day I'd run water through some type solar pond heaters.

100 ml vegetable oil

2 teaspoons salt

1 teaspoon pepper

15 ml butter

50 ml chopped fresh parsley

This rise in the air allows the Pacific Ocean to spill more water into the Gulf of Alaska. If the temperature of the waters in the eastern tropical Pacific warms, then the trade winds decrease.
